children: , the chip designer, agreed to buy World Labs for about $8.2 billion in stock. Shares rose about 1.3% to $615.69 around 9:49 a.m. ET Tuesday, trimming their gain from the opening bell.

The deal brings Fei-Fei Li's spatial AI research into AMD. World Labs builds models that can reason about three-dimensional environments, with potential uses in robotics and simulation. Li will become AMD's chief scientist when the deal closes, Reuters reported. That gives AMD a closer look at the workloads its future chips may need to run.

The valuation leaves little room for a vague AI payoff. At $615.685, the shares stood 114.98% above the chart's $286.39 GF Value estimate. World Labs could help AMD build better systems, but investors will want to see that research turn into products customers buy.

title: AMD Stock Rises as $8.2 Billion World Labs Bet Raises Bar
